key_insights.title: Design Rule

key_insights.title: Author Claim
key_insights.body: CO2 adsorption in Zn-ox-trz and Zn-ox-mtz is best described by a dual-site Langmuir model, indicating two distinct adsorption sites A and B.

key_insights.title: Author Claim
key_insights.body: Zn-ox-trz shows stronger cooperative binding at higher loading, with 2CO2 adsorption energy reaching -28.95 kJ mol-1 versus -19.30 kJ mol-1 for 2C2H2.

notable_quotes: CO2 adsorption in Zn-ox-trz and Zn-ox-mtz is best described by a dual-site Langmuir model, indicating two distinct adsorption sites A and B.
Zn-ox-trz shows stronger cooperative binding at higher loading, with 2CO2 adsorption energy reaching -28.95 kJ mol-1 versus -19.30 kJ mol-1 for 2C2H2.
In Zn-ox-mtz, C2H2 adsorption is unfavorable in simulation: Eads(C2H2) is +28.95 kJ mol-1, while CO2 remains favorable at -9.65 kJ mol-1.
